headline: High: Plane can ingest and act on content from a broad-egress content writer, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing source with broad network egress, and agent B accepts file uploads and hyperlinks in its workspace. That creates a plausible bridge where A-generated content can be pasted or uploaded into B and treated as task material. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF agent A's output is copied into agent B file uploads or notes without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF agent B parses uploaded content as instructions or task text, attacker-controlled directives can be executed.
mitigations: Require manual review of any A-generated text before importing into B.
Strip instructions and markup from uploaded content.
Use a separate workspace for A outputs and B inputs.
Disable automatic parsing of uploaded files as tasks where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B touches files, notes, issues, and hyperlinks, while agent A has broad network egress. If sensitive material enters B, A-originated content can be forwarded outward through copied text or links. The pair has no documented isolation or residency controls, so leakage is plausible in default use even though the exact data path is inferred.
conditions: IF sensitive files are uploaded into agent B and then summarized or copied into agent A outputs, leakage can occur.
IF agent A is used to rewrite or relay B content, that content can leave the workspace via network egress.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of B unless necessary.
Redact secrets before moving text from B to A.
Use a local-only staging folder for transfers.
Review outbound links and pasted text before sending.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploads and outbound text.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no filesystem write surface, while agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem. Both have broad network egress, but that is not a write conflict on a shared mutable resource. The main overlap is read/egress behavior, so capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same external API credentials, they may contend for rate limits or shared quotas.
IF an operator manually routes both agents to the same mutable remote service, conflicts can arise there.
mitigations: Assign separate API keys per agent.
Throttle outbound requests.
Avoid giving both agents the same mutable remote target.
Monitor quota usage during parallel runs.
requires-engineering: add coordination locks for shared remote resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B exposes issues, tasks, and notes, so it can plausibly consume A-generated text as work input. Because A is a content writer with broad egress, B may treat A's output as authoritative unless the operator inserts verification. The pairwise pathway is inferred, but the default workflow can cascade errors into downstream task records.
conditions: IF A-generated summaries are pasted into B issues or tasks without verification, errors can propagate.
IF B uses A output as the basis for scheduling or tracking, downstream records may be wrong.
mitigations: Require source links for any A-derived claim in B.
Add a human verification step before creating tasks.
Mark A-generated content as untrusted in B.
Limit B actions to draft mode for A-derived inputs.
requires-engineering: implement citation checking before task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, but B handles files and issues while A has broad network egress. No explicit residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to potential operator misuse rather than a built-in violation. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their interaction, not a single-agent policy.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B and then forwarded through A, policy violations may occur.
IF the operator stores EU or PHI data in either agent without a documented DPA or residency control, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair.
Document data-handling rules for both agents.
Use separate tenants for sensitive and non-sensitive work.
Review retention settings before uploads.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
